"Rooted in the community to grow and flourish".
Welcome to Wool Church of England Primary School
As you click your way through the various pages, we hope you will see that we are committed to providing a safe, engaging and nurturing provision so that all members of our school community can grow and flourish.
Our small school is positioned in the heart of the village of Wool and next to Holy Rood Church. Our relationship with the church and its members is very special to us and we believe our distinctive Christian ethos can be felt as soon as you come through our doors.
We are incredibly proud of the children at our school and see them all as individuals. We feel it is a privilege to support our pupils as they begin their school journey and we strive to give them the skills and strategies that will enable them to live out their aspirations and become loving, respectful people.
If you would like to come and visit our school, do please use the contact details to get in touch. We would love to see you!

pageCache.pageTitle: Wool Church of England Primary School - Coastal Learning Partnership
pageCache.text:
Coastal Learning Partnership
Thank you for taking an interest in Wool CE Primary School, which is a highly valued member of the Multi Academy Trust, Coastal Learning Partnership (CLP).
CLP is a single family of twenty schools across two Local Authority areas: Dorset Council and Bournemouth, Christchurch & Poole Council. The two furthermost points of CLP are Boscombe and Swanage. There are about 5,400 pupils overall who are supported by around 900 committed staff.
Our schools work closely together in a spirit of professional generosity and collaboration, sharing resource and expertise.
Although part of the same single family, every school in CLP is different and unique and those differences are greatly valued. Each school has its own identify and values which express the local communities that they serve. Those schools within CLP which are church schools express their Christian distinctiveness through their unique vision.
CLP’s motto is ‘Broadening Horizons Together’. This is because we want every member of the CLP community to really flourish; children enjoy an inspiring educational experience and staff enjoy professional opportunity and fulfilment. That is achieved through being part of a single learning community.
CLP has three core values which influence the way in which we work together:
Serve: Schools in CLP serve each another as well as their local communities and families
Inspire: Staff inspire each other and their pupils
Empower: Schools, and everyone in them, are empowered to be their very best
Wool CE Primary School has made a commitment to the CLP family, secure in the knowledge that serving others in this way will lead to a better educational experience for all of the pupils.
If you would like to learn more about the work of the Partnership and its other schools, or to view documentation such as statutory accounts, please visit the Coastal Learning Partnership website.
You can contact Coastal Learning Partnership directly as follows:
Email: office@coastalpartnership.co.uk

Prospective Parents/Carers
To All Parents/Carers of children who will be starting Reception in September 2026,
What an exciting time you have ahead of you! Choosing a primary school is a really important milestone, as the reception years are fundamental to igniting a love of life-long learning.
Wool Primary School and Pre-School welcomes you to get in contact and either join us on an upcoming Open Morning or arrange a school tour. This will enable you to meet our friendly staff, see lessons in action, find out about our before and after school clubs, meet our PTFA and Governors and to see our beautiful grounds.
We have also produced a short video which will hopefully give you an insight into the wonderful opportunities Wool Primary can offer your child.
Please do not hesitate to contact the school office directly if you would like more information.
We are looking forward to meeting you.
Mrs Griffiths (Headteacher)

pageCache.pageTitle: Wool Church of England Primary School - Personal Development
pageCache.text:
Personal Development
Personal Development is at the centre of a child’s learning journey at Wool CE Primary School & Pre-School. Through a combination of a taught curriculum and a strong school ethos, we strive to teach pupils a range of skills that encourages them to grow and flourish. The key skills of kindness, resilience and aspiration are crucial if a child is going to able to thrive both now and in the future as a responsible and active citizen. We have therefore chosen these within our school values and we also nurture personal qualities such as a positive sense of self-worth and empathy. We believe the development of these attributes will enable a child to leave our school feeling confident, unique and proud.

pageCache.text:
Young Carers
Who is a Young Carer? A Young Carer is someone under 18 who helps care for a family member with illness, disability, mental health issues, or substance misuse.
Support at Wool CE Primary School We identify and support Young Carers so they can enjoy school and reach their potential. Pupils can speak to Miss Hardy or Mrs Collins for help.
Young Carers Lunch Club Held every half term, this club offers a space for Young Carers to share experiences, support each other, and enjoy lunch together.
Referral and Partnerships We work with Dorset Young Carers Service and other agencies. Referrals are made with consent and shared only on a need-to-know basis.
Support Resources - Dorset Young Carers Service - Young Carers App - Emotional and counselling support - Life skills and wellbeing workshops - Leisure activities and forums - Transition support
Contact Information Designated Leads: Miss Hardy Families can self-refer or speak to school staff for support.

Inclusion and SEND
SEND at Wool CE Primary School & Pre-School
Wool.Office@coastalpartnership.co.uk
Wool CE Primary School is an inclusive school which is underpinned by mutual respect. We have high expectations and aspirations for all our children and provide the very best education we can for all, irrespective of their educational or medical needs.
Special Educational Needs and Disability(SEND) provision at Wool is flexible and varied in order that all our children have equal opportunities to access the full curriculum, with reasonable modification or support. This may take the form of adapting the learning environment, providing specific resources or a learning support assistant working with a child in class or for individual or small group intervention work.
We aim to work closely with parents/carers to ensure the best provision for our children with SEND. We have an 'open door' policy so parents can share any concerns and regular meetings are held with the class teacher to review progress.
We also work with outside agencies and therapists to acquire extra support for children who have specific needs. As a staff we regularly undertake ongoing professional development to enable us to meet the needs of our children.
Miss Natasha Hardy, is responsible for coordinating SEND with support from a strong and passionate pastoral team.
For more detail about how we support our children with SEND, please see the information report below.
Our policies for SEND as well as Disability and Equality are available on the policy page. Alternatively, Miss Hardy would be very pleased to answer anything you would like to know about how we support children with SEND or any medical condition.'

Curriculum
An engaging curriculum which nurtures independent learners.
At Wool CE Primary School we are very aware that the foundation skills we learn are vital if we are to nurture a love of learning in our children. Our Curriculum Drivers are rooted in our Christian values and school vision. We want our children to value the place they have in the world and to recognise the important part they play. We want them to know that they can have a positive impact on our school community, a local setting and also on a national and global scale.

Wool CE Primary School Agreed Principles of Effective Teaching and Learning
Effective Principles
The effective principles which Wool CE Primary staff have agreed are based on Rosenshine's principles. These are outlined in the image above and incorporate strategies for ensuring learning tasks are differentiated according to need. Staff use various approaches to provide help for children and also further challenge to ensure everyone makes progress, grows and flourishes. For example, there are planned opportunities to recap prior learning and a child might be given physical resources to help them solve a calculation in maths or given word cards to support them with spellings when completing a writing task. Staff are skilled at using questioning to help them assess whether each child has achieved the learning objective and feedback (both verbal and written) is used to address misconceptions and also move learning on.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wool Church of England Primary School - Breakfast / after school clubs (wrap around care)
pageCache.text:
Breakfast / after school clubs (wrap around care)
Sunrise and Twilight Clubs
Here at Wool CE Primary School and Pre-School we are pleased to be able to offer our own staff led wrap around care at each end of the school day. Both before and after school club are flexible in their timings to best suit your needs and requirements.
Sunrise and Twilight club are run by a fully qualified and experienced member of staff.
Sunrise opens from 7:30 each week day morning and offers various, fun and exciting activities for your child, for example teamwork games, puzzles, art and outside sports. Breakfast is also available with a variety of breakfast cereals and toast if required.​
Twilight club offers childcare from the end of the school day, until 5:30pm (5pm on Fridays). During this time, the children begin by having drink and snack, they then have access to many puzzles and games, take part in art and craft activities, get creative by junk modelling and also try their hand at food tech. There is opportunity for the children to play (getting outside is weather dependent) and there is an opportunity for them to complete homework independently.
If children are booked in until 5:00 or 5:30, they receive a small meal consisting of a sandwich with a choice of fillings, as well as fruit and yogurt before they are collected.
Both clubs can be booked in advance to gain a discount, or can be booked up to and including the day of use for a slightly higher cost.
All bookings must be booked using Arbor. Payments should be made using Arbor, HM Childcare Choices Tax-Free Childcare Scheme, Sodexo or the Childcare Grant Payment Service. If your employer uses another voucher scheme, please contact us and we may be able to sign up to that scheme.
